title: Choose Sahay's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Prescription Pad & Rubber Stamp. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Prescription Pad & Rubber Stamp
options.lineage: Indian clinic Rx pads, OPD slips, doctor's rubber stamps
options.thesis: Every answer is written on the clinic's pad and stamped only when it is checked.
options.viewport: Chat is a pad sheet: maroon letterhead strip with member + Rx glyph, answers as typed lines, citations as stamped reference codes, the verifier as a round stamp in the margin.
options.risk: Turns costume if the stamp and letterhead are used as decoration instead of as real states.

raised.raise: The current answer owns the sheet; older turns fold into a stub column, so one thing is read at a time.
Rank by weight and case, not size: three type sizes total across the whole product.
Flat unmodulated ink, zero drop shadows; separation is rules and paper only.
One big number per view (HbA1c 7.9) carries the hierarchy; everything else stays small.

options.label: The Pathology Report
options.lineage: Indian diagnostic lab printouts (letterhead, range column, bold H/L flags, pathologist signature)
options.thesis: Every screen is a signed report: value, range, flag, source, signature.
options.viewport: Health tab as a report: patient header block, tabular values with a range column and H/L flags, sparkline in the margin, a 'checked by verifier' signature block at the foot.
options.risk: The most familiar choice for health data; can read as a plain printout if the type is timid.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: jet-age airline ticket wallets, carbon coupons
options.thesis: Every order, claim and dose is a coupon that gets stamped, used or voided, never deleted.
options.viewport: Order + claim answers render as coupons; vaccine journey as a coupon book where used doses tear off.
options.case: Holds product clarity (honest states: validated, used, void); loses audience identification to the Rx pad.
options.risk: Travel metaphor is foreign to a health task; feels themed outside orders.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack the whole case onto one screen: tiny type, ruled modules, one red tab each.
options.viewport: Health and ops as a mosaic of ruled modules: meds, flags, labs, brief, traces all visible without scrolling.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the ops console; loses audience identification for older caregivers.
options.risk: Too dense for caregivers reading on a laptop at night.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.case: Fuses poorly: health records are tables, not media.
options.risk: Hides the source and the history.
options.kept: The current answer owns the sheet.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight, case and reversal.
options.case: Fuses poorly: raked panes fight long medical text.
options.kept: Rank by weight and case, not size.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Areas as flat swelling lobes of colour.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful map undercuts medical trust.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: the product is not about type.
options.kept: One big number per view carries the hierarchy.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean health-app dashboard, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, white cards with stats, chat in the center.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other health app by design.
